denial.carcText: The diagnosis is inconsistent with the procedure.
denial.text: Copperfield Health denied the claim for CPT 27447 (total knee arthroplasty) with date of service 2026-03-15. CARC 11: The diagnosis is inconsistent with the procedure. Payer remark: The diagnosis reported does not support the procedure billed.

criteria.text: Radiographic evidence of advanced osteoarthritis: Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4, joint space narrowing to bone-on-bone contact, or deformity.

Failure of at least 3 months of conservative treatment including anti-inflammatory or analgesic medication, physical therapy or a supervised home exercise program, activity modification, and at least one intra-articular corticosteroid injection.
Pain with weight-bearing that interferes with activities of daily living, with limited range of motion or instability on examination.
Body mass index under 40, nicotine-free, and medically optimized for surgery.

chart.text: Patient called about a tick bite on the scalp after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Blood pressure check. 137 over 81 today, 126 over 81 on repeat. He has been taking the lisinopril 10 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. He mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.

Here with a cough and congestion for 6 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if he gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.

58 year old man in orthopedic clinic for the left knee, hurting for 5 years and much worse this year. Discussed the options from more conservative care to replacement. His history otherwise: hypertension on lisinopril, mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Quit smoking 14 years ago, no alcohol, drives for a living. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Meloxicam 15 daily for the better part of a year, acetaminophen on top, gave up the yard work, uses a cane outdoors. Sending him to PT. Pain with every step, night pain that wakes him, cannot do stairs without the rail, cannot kneel or get out of a low chair without pushing up. Range of motion 5 to 105 degrees with crepitus, medial joint line tenderness, varus thrust with gait.

Standing AP, lateral, and sunrise views of the left knee. Complete loss of the medial joint space with bone-on-bone contact, large marginal osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis and cysts, 9 degrees of varus. Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4.
PT evaluation, left knee osteoarthritis. Quad strengthening, range of motion, gait training with the cane. Plan 8 weeks.
Session 2. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, he reports no real change.
Session 3. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, he reports no real change.
Intra-articular corticosteroid injection, left knee, triamcinolone 40 with lidocaine, anterolateral approach. Tolerated well.
Session 4. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, he reports slight improvement that does not last.
A1c came back 5.8. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. He is motivated.
Session 5. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, he reports about the same.
Session 6. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, he reports about the same.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 13 and 13. No ocular pathology noted.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

Back to decide on the left knee. Recommended total knee arthroplasty. Reviewed the operation, the hospital stay, the rehab, and the risks including infection and clot. Vitals today 124 over 86, pulse 75. Finished 8 weeks of PT, the injection gave about 3 weeks of relief, still on the meloxicam, still using the cane. That is 9 months of conservative care without durable benefit. BMI 35, never smoked, A1c 6.3, dental clearance in the chart.
He called asking where things stand with the insurance. Told him the paperwork went in and we are waiting to hear. Reviewed what to do in the meantime.
Interval visit. Nothing new since last time, symptoms as described before, he is managing. Went over the plan again and answered questions from his spouse.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 5 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
He called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in early summer. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Work note requested for a sick day last Monday. Faxed to the employer.
Pre-op. Medical clearance in the chart. Hold the meloxicam a week out. Consent signed for left total knee arthroplasty.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 11 denial can be answered from the record.
